texts: When the Council convenes, the Council redistributes mire-essence across the lantern-stations.
Whenever the Council meets, the Council reallocates mire-essence among the lantern-stations.
Productive stations contribute mire-essence to a central pool.
Burdened stations draw mire-essence from the central pool.
The Keepers record the redistribution in the Watch ledgers.

fields.sentence: When the Council convenes, the Council redistributes mire-essence across the lantern-stations.
parse: (: whenever_council_convenes_redistribute (Implication (And (Member $c convene) (Agent $c sk_council_1)) (And (Member (sk_redistribute $c) redistribute) (Agent (sk_redistribute $c) sk_council_1) (Theme (sk_redistribute $c) mire_essence) (Across (sk_redistribute $c) sk_group_1) (During (sk_redistribute $c) $c))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: The compound kind `mire_essence` gets no genus atom `(Inheritance mire_essence essence)`, which Compound concepts requires (head genus always emitted; the noun modifier `mire` correctly stays unexposed) — and the same parse does emit `(Inheritance lantern_station station)`, so the omission is inconsistent within one output.

review.notes: `Across` is licensed as a preposition-named oblique (the preposition actually used, never a Location/Goal near-fit), the definite plural 'the lantern-stations' correctly takes a group witness rather than Inheritance, and one `sk_council_1` symbol is reused across both clauses. Rule shape, Skolem-function event, During link, Theme for the displaced mass and the absence of a tense atom are all correct.

issues.reason: Compound concepts says the head genus 'is always emitted' for a compound kind you use and Core patterns lists a decomposed compound's genus among the always-licensed atoms, so `mire_essence` — a transparent modifier+head compound whose IS-A holds — must carry `(Inheritance mire_essence essence)`; its omission violates that rule (the parse itself emits the parallel `lantern_station` genus).

new_gaps: habitual 'when' with a definite participant ('When the Council convenes, ...'): the bare-'when' routing line legislates only indefinite participants -> rule and definite participants in a one-off narrative -> two ordered events; a definite participant in a present-tense regularity is assigned only by analogy with the whenever example's constant bell and dog
adjudication.defect_summary: Add the compound's genus atom `(Inheritance mire_essence essence) (STV 1.0 0.99)` beside the rule; every other atom stands.
adjudication.notes: The common-noun 'the Council' with no Name atom, one `sk_council_1` reused across both clauses, the `Across` oblique, the definite-plural group witness with its `lantern_station` genus, `Theme` for the displaced mass, the per-occurrence Skolem and `During` link are all correct.

fields.sentence: Whenever the Council meets, the Council reallocates mire-essence among the lantern-stations.
parse: (: council_meet_reallocate (Implication (And (Member $x meet) (Agent $x sk_council_1)) (And (Member (sk_reallocate $x) reallocate) (Agent (sk_reallocate $x) sk_council_1) (Theme (sk_reallocate $x) mire_essence) (Among (sk_reallocate $x) sk_stations_1) (During (sk_reallocate $x) $x))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

review.notes: "The Council" is correctly the capitalized-common-noun default (Member, no Name, no GroupOf, no distribution — a singular collective does not distribute), the definite plural "the lantern-stations" takes a group witness, and (Among ...) is the licensed preposition-named oblique for a PP that names neither where/when/how nor a listed role.

fields.sentence: Productive stations contribute mire-essence to a central pool.
parse: (: station_contribute (Implication (And (Member $x station) (Member $x productive)) (And (Member (sk_contribute $x) contribute) (Agent (sk_contribute $x) $x) (Theme (sk_contribute $x) mire_essence) (Recipient (sk_contribute $x) sk_pool_1))) (STV 0.9 0.9))

review.notes: 'a central pool' is read as one shared constant rather than a per-station Skolem function; 'central' plus Core patterns' world-knowledge-picks-the-reading makes that the favored reading rather than a genuine scope tie, so the first-quantifier-wide-scope tiebreaker does not apply. Recipient (not Goal) for 'to a central pool' follows the doctrine's 'goal of a transfer' definition, which imposes no animacy requirement, and the bare mass object mire_essence correctly stays a kind filler.

fields.sentence: Burdened stations draw mire-essence from the central pool.
parse: (: burdened_station_draw (Implication (And (Member $x station) (Member $x burdened)) (And (Member (sk_draw $x) draw) (Agent (sk_draw $x) $x) (Theme (sk_draw $x) mire_essence) (Source (sk_draw $x) sk_pool_1))) (STV 0.9 0.9))

review.notes: The adjectivally restricted bare-plural subject correctly forces the distributing rule with the restriction as a premise conjunct at 0.9/0.9 and no QuantifierPhrase, mire_essence gets its head genus with the noun modifier left unexposed, and the bare mass object stays a kind filler. Splitting 'the central pool' into two atoms rather than fusing central_pool is a defensible reading of the classifier-vs-description line.

fields.sentence: The Keepers record the redistribution in the Watch ledgers.

review.notes: "The Keepers" correctly takes the capitalized-plural-label treatment (Name-only individual, no GroupOf and no invented per-member kind) and "the Watch ledgers" the proper-noun-premodifier treatment (head phrase parsed normally as a definite plural group, linked by opaque Possession, no fused compound and no Name-string merge); record takes Theme per the evaluate/record carve-out, and the bare simple present correctly gets no status atom. The one debatable slot is (Location sk_record_1 sk_ledger_1) for "in the Watch ledgers" — a document medium rather than a place — though the PP does answer "where", which is the test the instruction set states.
